canonical_question: Is the 500 MPa yield strength threshold at 1200 °C the specific design limit that necessitates the coating strategy?

question_variants.question: Is the 500 MPa yield strength threshold at 1200 °C the specific design limit that necessitates the coating strategy?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper states that the yield strengths of the alloys are higher than 500 MPa at 1200 °C, implying they do not strictly fall below this threshold at this temperature, but the text suggests the threshold is a relevant design context for high-temperature applications.

answers.answer: The text confirms that the yield strengths of the RHEAs (and reference materials) remain higher than 500 MPa at 1200 °C. This suggests that while they meet the strength requirement, the coating strategy is driven by other factors, likely the 'poor oxidation resistance' mentioned as a major obstacle in the same context.
answers.mechanism: Not explicitly detailed in this span, but implies oxidation is the limiting factor despite adequate strength.
answers.boundary_limitation: No specific yield strength value is given, only a comparative threshold.
evidence_spans: The aim of this paper is to explore the feasibility of the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating in improving the oxidation resistance of MoNbTaTiW RHEA. The Si-20Cr-20Fe coating was prepared on the surface of MoNbTaTiW RHEA by a fused slurry method. To show the anti-oxidation mechanism of the silicide coating, the evolution of the structure and compositions of the coating at 1000 °C and 1300 °C were studied.

source_evidence_spans: Furthermore, their yield strengths are still higher than 500 MPa at 1200 °C [ [15] , [16] ].
